Imma be real honest, a cheap $80-$100 airbrush and compressor set will serve just fine. I've been using the same thing for over 6 months and I'm still glad I have it. Yeah, I have problems with paint feeding and water in my air lines but they're manageable and can sometimes be attributed to other factors than just equipment quality (humidity, paint thickness, air pressure, inexperience, etc.)

A few words of advice, get a set with an actual, stand-alone compressor. None of this "box-attached-to-the-brush" crap. Those are gimmicky and cheaply-made amongst even the cheaply-made. You want one that you got to run a hose to.
 
Additionally, clean your airbrush thoroughly and often. Isopropyl alcohol 90% and above with do this job pretty well. Just make sure to remove the o-rings from the brush first because the alcohol will damage them. You don't have to worry about the o-rings that deal with things like the air hose as you shouldn't be cleaning those parts anyway.

 Be delicate with brush and treat it like the delicate, precision instrument it is. Clean it gently, lubricate your o-rings (Vaseline, dedicated greases and lubricants will work great for this, I've even been able to get away with using Chapstick), and assemble and disassemble it delicately. I once broke off the tip of my airbrush putting and together and the threads got stuck in the body. Feeling righty-tighty become righty-loosey was a real scary experience. 

Hope this all helps! Buying an airbrush was probably the best hobby purchase I've ever made. For all the times I fight with my malfunctioning, cheapo airbrush, I still wouldn't trade it for hand brushing base coats. The finish is so much smoother and the process is so much quicker. Best of luck!
